description: The python library for real-time communication

summary.one_liner: FastRTC is a Python library that turns ordinary Python functions into real-time audio and video streams over WebRTC or WebSockets.
summary.what_it_does: The library wraps a Python handler function in a Stream object and serves it over WebRTC or WebSockets. ReplyOnPause adds automatic voice activity detection, so the handler is called after the user pauses and can yield audio back. Stream.ui.launch() opens a built-in Gradio interface for testing, and stream.mount(app) attaches the stream to a FastAPI app to provide WebRTC and WebSocket endpoints for a custom frontend. The README also describes a fastphone() method that gives a temporary phone number for audio-only calls, which requires a Hugging Face token. Optional extras add pause detection (vad) and text-to-speech (tts). The README includes examples for echo, LLM voice chat, webcam video flipping, and YOLOv10 object detection.
use_cases: add speech-to-text and text-to-speech to a web app
stream webcam video through a Python function
run object detection on a live webcam feed
add a phone-call interface to a Python app
mount a WebRTC endpoint on an existing FastAPI service
how_to_run: app = FastAPI(); stream.mount(app)  # then run: uvicorn app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
notable: ReplyOnPause provides built-in voice activity detection and turn taking
One Stream object can be exposed as a Gradio UI, a FastAPI WebRTC endpoint, a WebSocket endpoint, or a phone number
Examples cover Gemini, OpenAI realtime voice, Whisper, Claude, and Kyutai Moshi integrations
Handlers can be plain functions that yield audio or video frames
caveats: fastphone() requires a Hugging Face token and is audio only
Pause detection and text-to-speech need the optional vad and tts extras
The README is a shortened usage guide; full documentation is referenced but not included
